newsitem.title: UK: ICI says stg hitting UK exports, customers.
newsitem.headline: ICI says stg hitting UK exports, customers.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc said on Thursday the strong pound was hurting both its own exports from the UK and its British customer base.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief financial officer Alan Spall said in the first half of the year, "the UK has not been good."

"We think there is evidence now that (supports) the concerns about a strong pound and its impact on exports. It is affecting not only how our businesses do but also affecting our customer base in the UK," he said.
He said the pound, which was trading above 3.05 marks in early dealing on Thursday, "was well overvalued above three marks. We'd be much more comfortable in the 2.50 to 2.60 mark area."
Spall said ICI's sales volumes in the UK fell by five percent in the second quarter, and were down two percent in the first six months of the year.
He said this contrasted with a nine percent rise in sales in mainland Europe in the first half and a seven percent gain in the Americas.
Spall said the whole of the UK manufacturing base was now having "a difficult time."
"We are making general noises about sterling being overvalued and this being very unhelpful to manufacturing industry in the UK," he told Reuters.
